description:
Mailbox is the primary storage object. Four types with distinct semantics:

personal: one owner, per-user Sieve script allowed, block store write, JMAP visible, quota enforced
shared: ACL grantees, system Sieve only, block store write, JMAP visible, shared read state with per-identity flags
archive: write-once, read-only grants only, block store write, JMAP visible, retention-locked
relay: no persistent store, system Sieve only, redirect actions only, JMAP invisible, never writes to block store

Schema:
  mailboxes(mailbox_id PK, display_name, mailbox_type, owner_id nullable, quota_bytes nullable, min_trust_level, created_at)
  mailbox_addresses(mailbox_id FK, address, send_as bool, PRIMARY KEY (mailbox_id, address))

mailbox_addresses is informational for send-as authorization — actual routing is in Sieve. relay mailboxes have no mailbox_addresses rows and no mailbox_grants rows. fileinto targeting a relay mailbox is a runtime error. relay mailboxes do not appear in JMAP Mailbox/get responses.
title: design: mailbox types — personal, shared, archive, relay
